RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the May 6, 2008/Vaisakha 16, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
178
Special tourism status to Uttar
Pradesh and Uttarakhand
*561. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:
(a) the States which have been accorded
special tourism status;
(b) the funds allocated by Government
to each of such States during the last three
years, year-wise;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
accord special tourism status to Uttar
Pradesh and Uttarakhand;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) by when the decision is likely to be
taken in this regard?
Supply of gas through pipelines in the
country
*562. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
supply cooking gas to consumers through
pipelines in the country, particularly in
Jyotiba Phule Nagar and Moradabad in
Uttar Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the details of funds sanctioned/spent
so far and the time schedule fixed for the
completion of the scheme;
(d) the expected number of consumers
to be benefited under this scheme;
(e) whether gas cylinders are likely to
be taken from the consumers covered under
the scheme; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Requirement of chartered
accountants
†*563. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of chartered
accountants required in the country at
present;
(b) the total number of educational
institutions which provide education in the
discipline of chartered accountancy in the
country at present and the total number of
seats in these institutions;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

179
(c) the action being taken by
Government to provide education for the
discipline of chartered accountancy as per
demand in the country; and
(d) if not, whether Government would
take action to ensure availability of chartered
accountants as per demand?
Upgradation of Jharsuguda Airstrip
*564. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: W ill the Minister of
CIVIL A VIA TION be pleased to state:
(a) the progress of converting Jharsuguda
Airstrip into a regular airport; and
(b) the detailed action plan by the
Airports Authority of India (AAI),
projected investment and the expected date
of completion of the project?
Investment in R & D activities
*565. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) what is the investment both in
amount as well as in percentage in the
Research and Development (R&D)
activities of various Public Sector
Undertakings and institutes under the
Ministry;
(b) whether it is a fact that investment
in R&D is far below the level required for a
country aspiring to emerge as economic
super power;
(c) what are the general norms for
investment in R&D in various fields under
their control; and
(d) how this percentage of investment
is comparable with similar undertakings and
institutes of the developed countries?
Contractual workers in national
carriers
*566. SHRI PRABHAT: Will the
Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government owned Indian
Airlines and Air India are hiring manpower
for their works on the contractual basis;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the departments where this
manpower has been utilized?
Loan waiver scheme for farmers
*567. SHRI PRAKASH JAV ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether instructions have been
issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
for the loan waiver scheme announced in
the annual budget;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has taken any
decision regarding inclusion of farmers in
the scheme, who hold more than 2 hectares
of land;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Government has taken any
decision for inclusion of farmers in the
scheme who have taken loan from private
moneylenders; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?

180
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Closure of private company operated
petrol-pumps
†*568. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of petrol-pumps set up
by private companies in the country, so
far;
(b) whether it is a fact that the petrol-
pumps run by the private companies are
being closed down due to incurring of losses;
(c) if so, the number of petrol-pumps
that have been closed down from 1st
February, 2008 till date alongwith the
details thereof, company-wise and State-
wise; and
(d) the steps taken by Government so
that consumers do not suffer?
Agreement between NTPC and RIL
*569. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the present status of Reliance
Industries Limited (RIL) and National
Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC)
agreement for supply of natural gas to its
power plants;
(b) whether RIL had abandoned the
agreement reached with NTPC earlier; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government to ensure that the
agreement is honoured by both the  companies?
Contribution of petroleum sector to
Government exchequer
†*570. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an additional
contribution of Rs. 35,000 crore is likely
to be added to Government exchequer in
the year 2007-08 due to increase in prices
of crude oil in international market;
(b) if not, the estimate in this regard; and
(c) the total estimated amount likely to
be deposited in Government exchequer
from petroleum sector through various
taxes, cess, etc.?
Regulation of micro financial
agencies
*571. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is in the process of making a law called
Micro Finance Sector Development and
Regulation Bill to regulate micro financial
agencies in the country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Grant for construction of Narmada
Main Canal
*572. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is inclined to
provide special financial grant for
construction of Narmada Main Canal; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

181
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Losses to Indian carriers
†*573. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that most of the
airlines are running in losses;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has taken any
steps to bring these airlines out of the red;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether flights of Indian are
proposed to be linked to Raipur, the capital
of Chhattisgarh and Bhopal, the capital of
Madhya Pradesh?
Unutilized money with RBI
*574. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than
80,000 crore rupees of Government money
remain unutilized with the Reserve Bank
of India (RBI);
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken by
Government in this regard?
Import duty on newsprint
*575. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Indian Newspaper
Society (INS) has represented for scrapping
the proposed import duty on newsprint
and printing machinery which is straining
the fiscal viability of print media industry;
(b) whether the rapid growth of
electronic media has adversely affected the
prospects of print media which values
freedom of expression and probity in
governance; and
(c) whether to offer a level playing field
vis-a-vis electronic media, Government
would accede to the just demands of the
INS?
Sovereign Wealth Fund
*576. DR. E.M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is
contemplating to establish "Sovereign
Wealth Fund" as the country is having
surplus forex reserves to the extent of
$ 309.16 billion; and
(b) if so, what is the time bound
programme for the same?
Report of IFPRI on price control
measures
†*577. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the report released by the
International Food Policy Research
Institute (IFPRI) which states that the
steps taken by Government to control
import and export with a view to check
price rise are harmful for development;
(b) if so, on what basis the
Governmental steps have been termed as
harmful for development in the report;

182
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) whether Government agrees with the
views expressed in the report; and
(d) if so, what is the reaction of
Government thereto?
Technical snags in aircrafts in Air
India and Indian Airlines
†*578. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of flights affected due to
technical snags in the aircrafts of Air India
and Indian Airlines during the last one year;
(b) whether it is a fact that Air India's
flight number 111 from Amritsar to Delhi
had to land at Rajasansi airport due to
leakage of hydraulic oil;
(c) if so, the reasons for frequent
technical snags in aircrafts; and
(d) the steps Government is taking to
avoid the risk to life of passengers?
High level of fluoride and arsenic in
ground water
*579. SHRIMATI JAY A
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of
W ATER RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a recent study
by the Central Ground Water Board
(CGWB) had indicated that the ground
water in over 200 districts of the country
has a high level of fluoride and arsenic,
posing a big public-health hazard;
(b) whether it is also a fact that among
184 districts across 19 States, Rajasthan is
the worst placed with all its 32 districts at
risk, while Orissa and Gujarat have 18
districts in the danger list, as revealed in
the CGWB website; and
(c) if so, the steps Government has
taken to address the problem?
Cost overrun of pending projects
*580. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) how many projects, including the
joint ventures of the Ministry, its PSUs
and subordinate offices costing over
rupees 20 crore or moe are running behind
schedule;
(b) what are the reasons for the delay
and the total estimated cost overrun; and
(c) what are the changes proposed in
these projects to complete them
expeditiously and to save cost?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 30th April, 2008 Secretary-General.
V aisakha 10, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 564, 566, 573, 578,
Corporate Affairs : 563,
Culture : —
Finance : 567, 571, 574, 575, 576, 577,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises : —
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 562, 565, 568, 569, 570, 580,
Tourism : 561,
Water Resources : 572, 579.
183
MGIPMRND—1886RS—29.04.2007.
